title: 第 40 課｜哈密頓方程：把速度換成動量｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
用拉格朗日量描述力學，等於假定系統的狀態由廣義座標與廣義速度給定。但這不是唯一的選擇，用座標與動量來描述有實質上的好處，於是問題就成了：運動方程會變成什麼樣子？從一組獨立變數換到另一組，數學上叫做勒讓德變換。從拉格朗日量的全微分出發，每個座標一項、每個速度一項；按定義，對速度的導數就是廣義動量，而由拉格朗日方程，對座標的導數就是動量的變化率，所以全微分寫成 Σ ṗ dq 加上 Σ p dq̇。關鍵的一步是把第二組寫成 Σ p q̇ 的全微分減去 Σ q̇ dp，移到左邊並反號，於是出現一個新的量：H = Σ p q̇ 減去 L，這就是哈密頓量，也就是用座標與動量寫出來的能量。幾何上這正是勒讓德變換——把切線的斜率取為新變數，把截距取為新函數。在新的關係式 dH = − Σ ṗ dq + Σ q̇ dp 裡，獨立變數已經是座標與動量，所以直接讀出係數：速度是哈密頓量對動量的導數，動量的變化率是它對座標的導數的負值。這兩條就是哈密頓方程，也叫正則方程。拉格朗日方法裡的 s 條二階方程，被換成了 2s 條一階方程，而且因為這一對式子如此簡單對稱，才叫做正則。它們在相空間裡有很漂亮的意義：在座標與動量張成的平面上，每一點的哈密頓量導數都給定了行進方向，所以整個演化就是一個流。再看哈密頓量本身怎麼變：把它的全時間導數展開並代入正則方程，中間兩項剛好抵消，只剩下對時間的偏導數。所以哈密頓量若不顯含時間就守恆，這就是能量守恆；在相空間裡，代表點永遠留在同一條等能量曲線上。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 40 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 40 | Hamilton's Equations: Trading Velocities for Momenta | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
Writing mechanics with the Lagrangian assumes the state of a system is given by its generalised coordinates and velocities. That is not the only choice: describing it by coordinates and momenta has real advantages, so what do the equations of motion become? Passing from one set of independent variables to another is what mathematics calls a Legendre transformation. Start from the total differential of the Lagrangian, a term in each coordinate differential and a term in each velocity differential. By definition the derivative with respect to a velocity is the generalised momentum, and by Lagrange's equations the derivative with respect to a coordinate is the rate of change of that momentum, so the differential becomes the sum of p-dot d q plus the sum of p d q-dot. The key step is to write the second group as the differential of the sum of p times q-dot, minus q-dot times d p; moving that differential to the left-hand side and reversing the signs produces a new quantity, H equal to the sum of p q-dot minus L. This is the Hamiltonian, the energy of the system written in coordinates and momenta. Geometrically it is exactly the Legendre transform, taking the slope of the tangent as the new variable and the intercept as the new function. In the new relation, d H equals minus the sum of p-dot d q plus the sum of q-dot d p, the independent variables are the coordinates and the momenta, so the coefficients can be read off directly: the velocity is the derivative of the Hamiltonian with respect to the momentum, and the rate of change of the momentum is minus its derivative with respect to the coordinate. These are Hamilton's equations, also called the canonical equations. The s second-order equations of the Lagrangian treatment are replaced by two s first-order ones, and because the pair is so simple and symmetric they are called canonical. They have a lovely meaning in phase space, the plane spanned by the coordinate and the momentum: at every point the derivatives of the Hamiltonian fix the direction of travel, so the whole evolution is a flow. Finally, look at how the Hamiltonian itself changes. Expand its total time derivative and substitute the canonical equations: the two middle terms cancel exactly, leaving only the partial derivative with respect to time. So a Hamiltonian without explicit time dependence is conserved, which is conservation of energy, and in phase space the representative point stays for ever on one curve of constant energy.

Lesson 40 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
